correctness.rationale: Fix the diagonal vertex labels. On every edge with unequal labels the commutation equation uniquely solves for b's arrow coefficient given the vertex values of b. For equal labels this arrow coefficient is free; precisely those edges S with nonzero arrow coefficient in a impose equalities on b's vertex values. Consequently dim C_A(a)=m−|D|+n−r(S), where D consists of unequal-label edges and r(S)=n−k_G(S) over every finite field. Weight each active equal edge by q−1, and each remaining edge by 1 if equal or qz if unequal. Expanding the latter as qz+(1−qz)1_equal and counting equality assignments on S∪T gives exactly the displayed double sum. Dividing by q^c removes the only dependence on n beyond r(E). In a forest the vertex differences and edge coefficients are independent parameters once root labels are fixed, with one zero-rank pair and q²−1 rank-one pairs per edge. On a cycle the provisional independent-edge contribution is the trace of the transfer matrix power, with eigenvalues P_q(z) and 1−z; only S containing the whole cycle overcounts rank by one, requiring all its labels equal and coefficients nonzero. Correcting the q(q−1)^ell such choices gives the stated term, and pendant edges supply independent P_q(z) factors. This includes isolated vertices and the edgeless case; the invariant counts elements, not distinct adjoint operators. No uploaded code was executed; the universal proof, not the finite output, establishes correctness.
